nodes.label: Data Catalog Vocabulary (DCAT) Version 3
nodes.desc: Base standard. W3C Recommendation.

nodes.label: UK Cross-Government Metadata Exchange Model
nodes.desc: The endorsed model this profile evolves (release v0.1.0, last changed July 2024).

nodes.label: Recording metadata to describe critical data assets
nodes.desc: The core metadata the Data Asset Management Policy asks for. Its attributes are crosswalked to this profile.

nodes.label: Data Marketplace data catalogue metadata (JSON Schema and API)
nodes.desc: How the Data Marketplace exchanges records. Its properties are crosswalked.

nodes.label: Guidelines and best practices for making government datasets ready for AI
nodes.desc: Data and metadata quality is one of its four pillars.

nodes.label: UK GEMINI
nodes.desc: The UK standard for geospatial metadata. Geospatial publishers follow it as well as this profile.

nodes.label: HealthDCAT-AP Release 7
nodes.desc: Health extension for the European Health Data Space. Release 6 was deprecated on 24 April 2026.

nodes.label: GeoDCAT-AP 3.1.0
nodes.desc: Geospatial extension of DCAT-AP, aligned with DCAT-AP 3.0.1.

nodes.label: StatDCAT-AP
nodes.desc: Statistics extension of DCAT-AP. Version 3 in revision.

nodes.label: mobilityDCAT-AP
nodes.desc: Mobility extension for national access points for transport data.

nodes.label: MLDCAT-AP 3.0.0 and 3.1.0
nodes.desc: Machine learning extension: models, their training data and their evaluation, aligned with the EU AI Act.

nodes.label: DCAT-AP HVD 3.0
nodes.desc: Rules for describing EU high-value datasets.

nodes.label: Eclipse Dataspace Protocol
nodes.desc: Data space catalogues as DCAT, with usage control as ODRL policies. Version 1.0.0 in July 2025; 1.0.2 in September 2026.

nodes.label: Croissant 1.1
nodes.desc: Metadata for machine learning datasets, on top of schema.org, with provenance and responsible AI properties.

nodes.label: MEDIN discovery metadata standard
nodes.desc: Marine profile of UK GEMINI.

nodes.label: HDR UK Gateway schemata
nodes.desc: Metadata schema for health datasets on the HDR UK Gateway, with a weighted quality score.

nodes.label: Data Best Practice Guidance
nodes.desc: Energy sector data principles: Dublin Core metadata, presumed open, open data triage.

nodes.label: Code of Practice for Statistics
nodes.desc: The standard official statistics are produced to.

nodes.label: org-id.guide
nodes.desc: Lists of organisation identifier schemes, such as Companies House and the charity registers.

nodes.label: ckanext-dcat
nodes.desc: The CKAN extension that reads and writes DCAT and DCAT-AP, and can expose Croissant.

nodes.label: DDI Codebook 2.5
nodes.desc: Metadata for social science and survey data, used by data archives.

nodes.label: Dublin Core Metadata Element Set 1.1
nodes.desc: The 15 core elements.

nodes.label: Dataset
nodes.desc: A collection of data, published or curated by one organisation, available in one or more forms.

nodes.label: Data service
nodes.desc: A set of operations, such as an API, that gives access to one or more datasets or data processing functions.

nodes.label: Distribution
nodes.desc: A specific form of a dataset, such as a CSV file, a GeoPackage or an API response.

nodes.label: Dataset series
nodes.desc: A group of datasets published separately but sharing a subject and a method, such as each release of a census.

nodes.label: Catalogue
nodes.desc: A curated collection of metadata about datasets and data services.

nodes.label: Catalogue record
nodes.desc: A record in a catalogue about one dataset or data service, with its own dates.

nodes.label: Organisation
nodes.desc: An organisation that publishes, creates or is responsible for a resource. In this profile, never a person.

nodes.label: Contact point
nodes.desc: A team that can answer questions about a resource, with the routes to reach it.

nodes.label: Location
nodes.desc: A named area or a shape on the earth. Prefer the identifier of a standard area, such as a GSS code.

nodes.label: Period of time
nodes.desc: A period with a start date, an end date or both.

nodes.label: Checksum
nodes.desc: A value calculated from a file, used to check it has not changed.

nodes.label: Relationship
nodes.desc: How one resource relates to another.

nodes.label: Responsible role
nodes.desc: An organisation and the role it plays for a resource, such as data owner.

nodes.label: Missing value
nodes.desc: A statement that one property is empty on purpose, and why, modelled on the nil reasons of GML and INSPIRE.

nodes.label: Access rights
nodes.desc: Who can get the data, and on what terms.

nodes.label: Security classification
nodes.desc: Classifications and the main marking from the Government Security Classifications Policy (version 2.0, August 2024).

nodes.label: Personal data
nodes.desc: Whether the data contains information about identifiable living people (UK GDPR).

nodes.label: Sensitive data
nodes.desc: Kinds of information that need extra care beyond being personal.

nodes.label: Who can see this record
nodes.desc: Who may see the metadata record. Provisional, pending research (issue 5).

nodes.label: Licences
nodes.desc: Licences commonly used for UK public sector data, and a value for when no licence applies and an agreement is needed.

nodes.label: Update frequency
nodes.desc: The EU frequency vocabulary, which DCAT-AP uses, with the Dublin Core frequency terms the xGov MEM used.

nodes.label: Theme
nodes.desc: The 14 data.gov.uk topics (read on 6 November 2026), each mapped to the EU data themes used by DCAT-AP.

nodes.label: Service status
nodes.desc: Phases of a service, from the Service Manual.

nodes.label: Interface style
nodes.desc: The style of interface a data service offers. Use conformsTo for the exact standard.

nodes.label: Language
nodes.desc: Languages of the UK and Ireland in the EU language vocabulary. Any other EU language code may also be used.

nodes.label: Responsible role
nodes.desc: Roles an organisation can play for a resource. Roles, never people.

nodes.label: Jurisdictions
nodes.desc: Countries and territories where data may be held, processed or sent, including the UK nations, the Crown Dependencies, the British Overseas Territories, the Commonwealth, the EEA and others.

nodes.label: Transfer safeguards
nodes.desc: The bases in UK GDPR for sending personal data outside the UK, as the ICO guidance of 15 January 2026 sets them out (provenance S).

nodes.label: Checksum algorithms
nodes.desc: Algorithms in the SPDX list for checking a file has not changed, with this profile's advice on each for long-term and quantum-era trust.

nodes.label: Connection security
nodes.desc: The key exchange a service's endpoint uses to protect data in transit, for the post-quantum migration inventory.

nodes.label: Reasons a value is missing
nodes.desc: Why a property is empty on purpose. Based on the nil reasons of GML 3.2 and the INSPIRE void reasons, so records can be mapped to geospatial and allied metadata that use the same idea.

nodes.label: Title
nodes.desc: The name of the resource, in plain English.

nodes.label: Description
nodes.desc: A plain English account of what the resource contains and what it can be used for.

nodes.label: Summary
nodes.desc: A one-sentence summary of the resource, of no more than 250 characters.

nodes.label: Alternative title
nodes.desc: Another name the resource is known by, such as an abbreviation or a former name.

nodes.label: Identifier
nodes.desc: The main identifier of the resource in the publisher's own catalogue.

nodes.label: Other identifier
nodes.desc: Any other identifier the resource is known by, such as one in a national or sector register.

nodes.label: Publisher
nodes.desc: The organisation responsible for making the resource available.

nodes.label: Creator
nodes.desc: The organisation that created or compiled the content of the resource.

nodes.label: Contact point
nodes.desc: Where to ask questions about the resource or give feedback on it.

nodes.label: Access rights
nodes.desc: Who can get the data, and on what terms.

nodes.label: Rights statement
nodes.desc: A statement of any restriction on access or use, such as the data sharing agreement or legal gateway needed.

nodes.label: Security classification
nodes.desc: The classification under the Government Security Classifications Policy that the data itself carries.

nodes.label: Personal data
nodes.desc: Whether the data contains information about identifiable living people, and in what form.

nodes.label: Sensitive data
nodes.desc: Whether the data contains information that needs extra care beyond being personal, such as special category data.

nodes.label: Who can see this record
nodes.desc: Who is allowed to see the metadata record itself.

nodes.label: Licence
nodes.desc: The licence under which the resource can be used.

nodes.label: Release date
nodes.desc: The date the resource was first made available.

nodes.label: Last updated
nodes.desc: The date the content of the resource last changed.

nodes.label: Created
nodes.desc: The date the content of the resource was created or compiled.

nodes.label: Update frequency
nodes.desc: How often the resource is updated.

nodes.label: Theme
nodes.desc: The broad subject of the resource, from a controlled list.

nodes.label: Keyword
nodes.desc: Words or short phrases that people might search for, not already in the title or description.

nodes.label: Geographic coverage
nodes.desc: The geographic area the data is about.

nodes.label: Spatial resolution (metres)
nodes.desc: The smallest distance the data can tell apart, in metres.

nodes.label: Time period covered
nodes.desc: The period of time the data is about.

nodes.label: Time resolution
nodes.desc: The smallest period the data can tell apart, as an ISO 8601 duration.

nodes.label: Conforms to
nodes.desc: A standard, specification or schema the resource follows.

nodes.label: Reference data used
nodes.desc: A code list, classification or set of groupings the data uses, such as age bands or a geography.

nodes.label: Version
nodes.desc: The version of the resource.

nodes.label: Version notes
nodes.desc: What changed in this version.

nodes.label: Previous version
nodes.desc: The version this one replaces in a sequence.

nodes.label: Replaced by
nodes.desc: A newer resource that replaces this one.

nodes.label: Expires
nodes.desc: The date after which the resource should no longer be used.

nodes.label: Part of series
nodes.desc: The dataset series this dataset belongs to.

nodes.label: Distribution
nodes.desc: A form in which the data can be got, such as a file or an API.

nodes.label: Related resource
nodes.desc: Another resource closely related to this one, such as the report the data supports.

nodes.label: Qualified relation
nodes.desc: A related resource together with the kind of relationship.

nodes.label: Landing page
nodes.desc: A web page where people can find out about the resource and how to get it.

nodes.label: Documentation
nodes.desc: A web page that documents the resource, such as a user guide or a methodology.

nodes.label: Language
nodes.desc: The language or languages of the resource.

nodes.label: Interface style
nodes.desc: For a data service, the kind of interface.

nodes.label: Status
nodes.desc: Where a data service is in its life, from discovery to retirement.

nodes.label: Data quality
nodes.desc: A link to a published statement or measurement of the quality of the data.

nodes.label: Critical data asset
nodes.desc: Whether the resource is a critical data asset under the Data Asset Management Policy.

nodes.label: Responsible role
nodes.desc: An organisation and the role it plays for the resource, such as data owner or data steward.

nodes.label: Access address
nodes.desc: A web address that gives access to the distribution, such as a landing page, a download page or an API.

nodes.label: Download address
nodes.desc: A direct link to a file.

nodes.label: Media type
nodes.desc: The file format, as an IANA media type.

nodes.label: Format
nodes.desc: The file type, from the EU file type list, where there is no IANA media type.

nodes.label: Size (bytes)
nodes.desc: The size of the file in bytes.

nodes.label: Checksum
nodes.desc: A value that lets people check the file they downloaded is complete and unchanged.

nodes.label: Access service
nodes.desc: A data service that gives access to this distribution.

nodes.label: Compression format
nodes.desc: The format the file is compressed in, as an IANA media type.

nodes.label: Endpoint address
nodes.desc: The root address of the service.

nodes.label: Endpoint description
nodes.desc: A description of what the service does and how to call it, such as an OpenAPI document.

nodes.label: Serves dataset
nodes.desc: A dataset this service gives access to.

nodes.label: Dataset
nodes.desc: A dataset listed in the catalogue.

nodes.label: Data service
nodes.desc: A data service listed in the catalogue.

nodes.label: Home page
nodes.desc: The home page of the catalogue or the organisation.

nodes.label: Theme list used
nodes.desc: The list of themes the catalogue uses to classify its records.

nodes.label: Catalogue record
nodes.desc: A record describing an entry in the catalogue.

nodes.label: Describes
nodes.desc: The dataset or data service this record describes.

nodes.label: Name
nodes.desc: The name of the organisation.

nodes.label: Organisation type
nodes.desc: The kind of organisation, as GOV.UK lists it, for example ministerial department or executive agency.

nodes.label: Team name
nodes.desc: The name of the team to contact. Never a person's name.

nodes.label: Contact form
nodes.desc: The address of a contact form or contact page for the team.

nodes.label: Team email address
nodes.desc: A shared team mailbox, as a mailto address. Never a personal address.

nodes.label: Telephone
nodes.desc: A team telephone number.

nodes.label: Postal address
nodes.desc: A postal address for the team.

nodes.label: Bounding box
nodes.desc: The rectangle that contains the area, as Well-Known Text in WGS 84.

nodes.label: Geometry
nodes.desc: The exact shape of the area, as Well-Known Text.

nodes.label: Centre point
nodes.desc: The centre point of the area, as Well-Known Text.

nodes.label: Place name
nodes.desc: The name of the place, from a gazetteer where there is one.

nodes.label: Start date
nodes.desc: The first day the data covers.

nodes.label: End date
nodes.desc: The last day the data covers.

nodes.label: Algorithm
nodes.desc: The algorithm used to calculate the checksum, from the SPDX list.

nodes.label: Checksum value
nodes.desc: The checksum, in lower-case hexadecimal.

nodes.label: Role
nodes.desc: The role in the relationship or attribution.

nodes.label: Organisation
nodes.desc: The organisation that plays the role.

nodes.label: Applicable legislation
nodes.desc: Legislation that requires, governs or permits the publication or sharing of the resource.

nodes.label: Usage policy
nodes.desc: A machine-readable policy, in the W3C Open Digital Rights Language (ODRL), saying what may and may not be done with the resource.

nodes.label: Where the data is held or sent
nodes.desc: Every country or territory where the data is stored or processed, or to which it is sent.

nodes.label: Transfer safeguard
nodes.desc: The basis under UK GDPR on which personal data in the resource may be sent outside the UK.

nodes.label: Connection security
nodes.desc: The kind of key exchange the service's endpoint uses to protect data in transit, classical or post-quantum.

nodes.label: Missing value
nodes.desc: A property this record leaves empty on purpose, and why.

nodes.label: Property left empty
nodes.desc: The property that has no value, as its prefixed name or full IRI.

nodes.label: Why it is empty
nodes.desc: The reason the property has no value, from a list based on the GML and INSPIRE nil reasons.

nodes.label: Source record
nodes.desc: The original metadata record this record was harvested or converted from.

nodes.label: Property added or changed on the way
nodes.desc: A property whose value was added or changed by the harvester or converter, rather than taken from the source record.

nodes.label: R-01: A contact point must give a contact form, a team mailbox, or both.
nodes.desc: A contact point must give a contact form, a team mailbox, or both.

nodes.label: R-02: A period of time must have a start date, an end date, or both.
nodes.desc: A period of time must have a start date, an end date, or both.

nodes.label: R-03: When access rights are commercial or internal, give a rights statement saying how to ask for the data.
nodes.desc: When access rights are commercial or internal, give a rights statement saying how to ask for the data.

nodes.label: R-04: When the record describes a critical data asset, the properties marked mandatory for critical data assets must be given.
nodes.desc: When the record describes a critical data asset, the properties marked mandatory for critical data assets must be given.

nodes.desc: The summary must be 250 characters or fewer.

nodes.label: R-07: A period's end date must not be before its start date.
nodes.desc: A period's end date must not be before its start date.

nodes.label: R-08: When the data contains personal data and is held in or sent to anywhere outside the UK, give the transfer safeguard.
nodes.desc: When the data contains personal data and is held in or sent to anywhere outside the UK, give the transfer safeguard.

nodes.label: Issue 78: Rename the repository and references to DCAT Application Profile for the UK
nodes.desc: A new repository, as the discussion suggested for a completely new solution: the model is no longer generated with LinkML and the site is no longer MkDocs. The old repository can be archived with a pointer here (ADR 0001

nodes.label: Issue 76: Title examples in alternative title don't follow the rules for titles
nodes.desc: Examples now follow the sentence case rule they illustrate, and a check fails the build if an example title is in title case.

nodes.label: Issue 72: Distribution is incorrectly configured as an IRI or CURIE
nodes.desc: A distribution can now be described in the same record or referred to by its IRI. The SHACL shape and JSON Schema both accept either.

nodes.label: Issue 71: The contact point definition is the same as the email definition
nodes.desc: Contact point is now defined as the contact as a whole. Team name, contact form and team mailbox each have their own definitions. A contact form is the preferred route; a team mailbox is allowed; a named person is not.

nodes.label: Issue 70: Launch release management, lock the specification and start formal change management

nodes.label: Issue 69: The OS postcodes example names the wrong publisher
nodes.desc: The example is rebuilt from the public record and credits Ordnance Survey as publisher and creator.

nodes.label: Issue 63: Codelist pages don't link out to external vocabularies
nodes.desc: The portal is generated by this repository's own script, so every concept links to its scheme and to the matching EU concept. The LinkML limitation no longer applies.

nodes.label: Issue 60: Add usage notes to access rights
nodes.desc: Usage notes for each value, the difference from licence and security classification, and a rights statement for anything not open.

nodes.label: Issue 49: Recommend a taxonomy for theme values
nodes.desc: The 14 data.gov.uk topics are the theme list, as the issue proposed, each with a readable identifier rather than a search address, and mapped to the EU data themes. The cross-government taxonomy can replace it when publi

nodes.label: Issue 44: What to do if there is no applicable licence
nodes.desc: The "data sharing agreement required" value is restored, with a rights statement to describe the agreement.

nodes.label: Issue 30: What to do with assets that don't have a modified date
nodes.desc: Last updated is recommended, not mandatory, and must never be invented. The created and release dates cover the rest.

nodes.label: Issue 26: Indicate whether the data includes sensitive information
nodes.desc: A sensitive data property with a codelist (special category, criminal offence, children, commercially sensitive, security sensitive).

nodes.label: Issue 25: Indicate whether the data includes personal identifiable information
nodes.desc: A personal data property, mandatory for critical data assets, with values for none, personal, pseudonymised, anonymised and not yet known.

nodes.label: Issue 15: Add a home page for the point of contact
nodes.desc: The contact point takes a web address (vcard:hasURL), which is also the preferred route as a contact form.

nodes.label: Issue 13: Decide on a persistent identifier for the metadata model

nodes.label: Issue 11: Include schemas in the documentation site
nodes.desc: JSON Schema, SHACL, JSON-LD context, LinkML, SKOS codelists, CSV and examples in Turtle and JSON-LD are all downloadable, with a DCAT description of them.

nodes.label: Issue 3: Capture the reference data used and its resolution
nodes.desc: A provisional "reference data used" property that links to the classification or code list (for example age bands) and its version.

nodes.desc: Time period covered (dct:temporal) with start and end dates, as the discussion recommended, plus time resolution and dataset series for repeated releases such as a census.

nodes.label: A catalogue (synthetic)
nodes.desc: The catalogue record that a harvester reads first, declaring that it conforms to this profile.

nodes.label: Health and care extension
nodes.desc: Describes health and care data well enough for a researcher or analyst to judge it before asking: who is covered, how many records, which clinical codes, and how access is controlled.

nodes.label: Health category
nodes.desc: The category of health data, such as electronic health records, registries or genomic data.

nodes.label: Health theme
nodes.desc: A disease, condition or topic the data is about, as an identifier.

nodes.label: Population covered
nodes.desc: Who is in the data, in words, such as "patients registered with a GP practice in Wales".

nodes.label: Number of records
nodes.desc: How many records the data holds, rounded.

nodes.label: Number of people
nodes.desc: How many different people the data is about, rounded and subject to disclosure control.

nodes.label: Youngest typical age
nodes.desc: The youngest age, in years, typical of people in the data.

nodes.label: Oldest typical age
nodes.desc: The oldest age, in years, typical of people in the data.

nodes.label: Clinical coding system
nodes.desc: A coding system used in the data, such as SNOMED CT, ICD-10, OPCS-4 or the Dictionary of medicines and devices.

nodes.label: National data opt-out applied
nodes.desc: Whether patients' national data opt-out choices have been applied to the data (England).

nodes.label: Trusted research environment
nodes.desc: The web page of the trusted research environment or secure data environment where approved people can use the data.

nodes.label: health without period
nodes.desc: Deliberate break of the health and care extension; must fail rule M-01

nodes.label: Geospatial extension
nodes.desc: Adds what GeoDCAT-AP and UK GEMINI ask for: coverage, coordinate reference system, resolution, topic category and lineage, so geospatial records can sit in the same catalogue as everything else.

nodes.label: Topic category
nodes.desc: An ISO 19115 topic category, such as boundaries, transportation or environment.

nodes.label: Lineage
nodes.desc: How the data was made, from what sources, and the processes applied.

nodes.label: Spatial representation type
nodes.desc: How the geographic information in this distribution is represented, such as vector or grid, from the INSPIRE list that GeoDCAT-AP uses.

nodes.label: Purpose
nodes.desc: Why the data was made.

nodes.label: Statement
nodes.desc: The lineage, in words.

nodes.label: geo without crs
nodes.desc: Deliberate break of the geospatial extension; must fail rule M-01

nodes.label: geo bad representation
nodes.desc: Deliberate break of the geospatial extension; must fail rule V-01

nodes.label: Official statistics extension
nodes.desc: Says what status the statistics have under the Code of Practice, and describes their dimensions and measures so tables can be found by what they count, as StatDCAT-AP does.

nodes.label: Statistics status
nodes.desc: The status of the statistics under the Code of Practice for Statistics.

nodes.label: Dimension
nodes.desc: A dimension the statistics are broken down by, such as area, age or year, as an identifier.

nodes.label: Measure
nodes.desc: What the statistics count or measure, as an identifier.

nodes.label: Attribute
nodes.desc: An attribute of the observations, such as a unit or a status flag, as an identifier.

nodes.label: Number of series
nodes.desc: How many time series the dataset holds.

nodes.label: stats without status
nodes.desc: Deliberate break of the official statistics extension; must fail rule M-01

nodes.label: stats bad status
nodes.desc: Deliberate break of the official statistics extension; must fail rule V-01

nodes.label: Transport and mobility extension
nodes.desc: Says which mode of transport, which network and which data standard (TransXChange, NeTEx, SIRI, GTFS, DATEX II) a dataset uses, as mobilityDCAT-AP does for European national access points.

nodes.label: Mobility theme
nodes.desc: The kind of mobility data, such as timetables, real-time arrivals or road works, from the mobilityDCAT-AP vocabulary.

nodes.label: Transport mode
nodes.desc: The mode of transport, such as bus, rail or cycling.

nodes.label: Network covered
nodes.desc: The part of the network covered, such as the strategic road network.

nodes.label: Georeferencing method
nodes.desc: How locations are referenced, such as coordinates or a location referencing method.

nodes.label: Mobility data standard
nodes.desc: The data standard of the file or feed, such as TransXChange, NeTEx, SIRI, GTFS or DATEX II.

nodes.label: transport without theme
nodes.desc: Deliberate break of the transport and mobility extension; must fail rule M-01

nodes.label: High-value datasets (for EU exchange) extension
nodes.desc: Adds the two properties the DCAT-AP high-value datasets profile requires, so UK records can be harvested by EU catalogues that report under the EU high-value datasets regulation.

nodes.label: High-value dataset category
nodes.desc: The category of high-value dataset, from the EU high-value dataset categories vocabulary.

nodes.label: hvd without legislation
nodes.desc: Deliberate break of the high-value datasets (for eu exchange) extension; must fail rule M-01

nodes.label: AI-ready extension
nodes.desc: Makes the record answer the questions an AI team asks first: may we train on it, is it synthetic, where is the data card, what policy applies, how good is it, and what period does it cover.

nodes.label: Use for AI
nodes.desc: Whether the data may be used to train, fine-tune or evaluate AI models.

nodes.label: Data card
nodes.desc: A page that documents how the data was collected, what it contains, what it is for and its known gaps and biases.

nodes.label: Synthetic data
nodes.desc: Whether the data was generated rather than collected.

nodes.label: Generated by
nodes.desc: The process, model or system that generated the data, as an identifier.

nodes.label: ai without use
nodes.desc: Deliberate break of the ai-ready extension; must fail rule M-01

nodes.label: ai bad use
nodes.desc: Deliberate break of the ai-ready extension; must fail rule V-01

nodes.label: Data spaces extension
nodes.desc: Follows the Dataspace Protocol catalogue rules: every dataset carries a machine-readable usage policy, every distribution names the service that gives it, and the catalogue names its participant.

nodes.label: Participant identifier
nodes.desc: The identifier of the data space participant that provides the catalogue.

nodes.label: dataspace without policy
nodes.desc: Deliberate break of the data spaces extension; must fail rule M-01

nodes.label: Private and voluntary sector extension
nodes.desc: GOV.UK organisation addresses only cover government. This extension asks for a registered identifier for every organisation, in the org-id.guide form, so a charity in Scotland, a company in Northern Ireland and a council

nodes.label: org bad identifier
nodes.desc: Deliberate break of the private and voluntary sector extension; must fail rule P-01

nodes.label: Energy extension
nodes.desc: Records the open data triage outcome for presumed-open energy system data, and asks for the Dublin Core elements the guidance requires. Every Dublin Core element already has a DCAT-AP-UK property.

nodes.label: Open data triage outcome
nodes.desc: The outcome of open data triage for data that is presumed open.

nodes.label: Presumed open
nodes.desc: Whether the data falls under the presumed open principle.

nodes.label: energy without triage
nodes.desc: Deliberate break of the energy extension; must fail rule M-01

nodes.label: Geodesy extension
nodes.desc: A candidate module on top of the geospatial extension. It says which reference frame and epoch the coordinates are in, how they were observed, and how uncertain they are, so precise positions are not silently mixed acros

nodes.label: Reference frame
nodes.desc: The coordinate reference system or terrestrial reference frame, and its realisation, that the coordinates are given in.

nodes.label: Coordinate epoch
nodes.desc: The date the coordinates refer to, as a decimal year, for frames in which positions move over time.

nodes.label: Vertical reference
nodes.desc: The height system the vertical values use, such as a national height datum or the ellipsoid.

nodes.label: Observation technique
nodes.desc: How the positions or heights were observed.

nodes.label: Horizontal uncertainty (metres)
nodes.desc: The typical horizontal uncertainty of the positions, in metres, at the confidence level given.

nodes.label: Vertical uncertainty (metres)
nodes.desc: The typical vertical uncertainty, in metres, at the confidence level given.

nodes.label: Confidence level (per cent)
nodes.desc: The confidence level the uncertainties are stated at, as a percentage, such as 95.

nodes.label: geodesy without frame
nodes.desc: Deliberate break of the geodesy extension; must fail rule M-01

nodes.label: geodesy bad technique
nodes.desc: Deliberate break of the geodesy extension; must fail rule V-01

nodes.label: CKAN with ckanext-dcat crosswalk
nodes.desc: Field names as the ckanext-dcat European profile reads and writes them. Fields marked extras are stored as CKAN extras or scheming fields.

nodes.label: Dublin Core (15 elements) crosswalk
nodes.desc: Required by Ofgem Data Best Practice for energy system data. Every element has a DCAT-AP-UK property, so a DCAT-AP-UK record is also a Dublin Core description.

nodes.label: UK GEMINI 2.3 crosswalk
nodes.desc: UK GEMINI is encoded in ISO 19139 XML. Properties from the geospatial extension are marked. A first step towards closing open register O-11, which needs the geospatial community.

nodes.label: HDR UK Gateway schema crosswalk
nodes.desc: Field paths as in the HDR UK schemata. Properties from the health extension are marked. The HDR UK schema allows an email contact; DCAT-AP-UK prefers a contact form.

nodes.label: Croissant 1.1 (ML datasets) crosswalk
nodes.desc: Croissant describes datasets for machine learning on top of schema.org. DCAT-AP-UK fills its dataset-level part; record sets (the columns and their types) are added with Croissant tools. The record builder exports this p

nodes.label: DDI Codebook (study level) crosswalk
nodes.desc: The study-level elements most used to describe social science and survey data. The weaver reads and writes them as JSON with the element names as keys.

nodes.label: D-004: The duplicate-title check missed a real duplicate.
nodes.desc: Cause: It read every <title> on the page, including the titles inside SVG images, so two pages never matched. Check: tools/check_site.py C-13 and its deliberate break

nodes.label: D-009: Loading the critical data asset example into the record builder lost its licence.
nodes.desc: Cause: The example used the compact form of the licence value; the licence list holds full addresses, so no option matched. Check: tools/check_browser.py: the critical data asset example must conform in the builder

nodes.label: D-014: An unknown property name with a space crashed the Turtle export instead of being reported.
nodes.desc: Cause: The name was used in an address without being encoded. Check: tests/test_toolkit.py test_unknown_key_with_space_serialises

nodes.label: D-015: The record builder’s Turtle dropped every property of a distribution that had its own address.
nodes.desc: Cause: A nested node with an address was written as the address alone. Check: tests/test_toolkit.py test_turtle_matches_python: browser Turtle and build RDF must be isomorphic for every example

nodes.label: D-029: LinkML's own validator rejected every worked example, so the LinkML file disagreed with the SHACL, JSON Schema and portal validators.
nodes.desc: Cause: The generated schema had no id slot, treated every link as a bare reference, and listed codes where records use compact or full IRIs. Nothing ran LinkML tools on it. Check: tools/check_linkml.py, with its --break,

nodes.label: RQ-01: Records can be exchanged with international and allied DCAT-based profiles without bespoke
nodes.desc: Records can be exchanged with international and allied DCAT-based profiles without bespoke translation for each pair.

nodes.label: RQ-02: Finding a record never grants access to the data. Who may have the data is stated separate
nodes.desc: Finding a record never grants access to the data. Who may have the data is stated separately from who may see the record.

nodes.label: RQ-03: A catalogue record can say how the record itself must be handled, separately from the hand
nodes.desc: A catalogue record can say how the record itself must be handled, separately from the handling of the data it describes.

nodes.label: RQ-04: A record can say why a property is empty (unknown, withheld, not applicable, not collected
nodes.desc: A record can say why a property is empty (unknown, withheld, not applicable, not collected or not yet available), so a strict harvester need not guess.

nodes.label: RQ-05: Validation is machine-readable and gives one verdict wherever it runs.
nodes.desc: Validation is machine-readable and gives one verdict wherever it runs.

nodes.label: RQ-06: Conformance is claimed by level and by layer, and only after the matching tests pass.
nodes.desc: Conformance is claimed by level and by layer, and only after the matching tests pass.

nodes.label: RQ-07: Specialist terms live in their own namespaces, as modules that can be required or left out
nodes.desc: Specialist terms live in their own namespaces, as modules that can be required or left out as a whole.

nodes.label: RQ-08: The authoritative source of a record, and of each value changed on the way, survives harve
nodes.desc: The authoritative source of a record, and of each value changed on the way, survives harvesting and mapping.

nodes.label: RQ-09: Every mapping says what it loses.
nodes.desc: Every mapping says what it loses.

nodes.label: RQ-10: Asset, dataset, data product, data service and distribution have one meaning each, which p
nodes.desc: Asset, dataset, data product, data service and distribution have one meaning each, which policy and catalogues share.

nodes.label: RQ-11: Organisations without an enterprise catalogue can still describe their assets, from a spre
nodes.desc: Organisations without an enterprise catalogue can still describe their assets, from a spreadsheet, and be found.

nodes.label: RQ-12: The profile works with the catalogue platforms departments already run, through configurat
nodes.desc: The profile works with the catalogue platforms departments already run, through configuration or adapters.

nodes.label: RQ-13: Validation works in disconnected and air-gapped environments, with no calls to the network
nodes.desc: Validation works in disconnected and air-gapped environments, with no calls to the network.

nodes.label: RQ-14: The public profile describes OFFICIAL information only. Anything needing higher classifica
nodes.desc: The public profile describes OFFICIAL information only. Anything needing higher classifications is handled in controlled layers.

nodes.label: RQ-15: Where allied exchange needs it, DCAT-AP-UK maps to the NATO Core Metadata Specification an
nodes.desc: Where allied exchange needs it, DCAT-AP-UK maps to the NATO Core Metadata Specification and its confidentiality labelling.

nodes.label: RQ-16: Geospatial records reference GEMINI rather than repeat it.
nodes.desc: Geospatial records reference GEMINI rather than repeat it.

nodes.label: RQ-17: Catalogues and information asset registers work together without becoming two registers of
nodes.desc: Catalogues and information asset registers work together without becoming two registers of the same things.

nodes.label: RQ-18: Public artefacts never expose controlled semantics, and never name people or meetings from
nodes.desc: Public artefacts never expose controlled semantics, and never name people or meetings from internal engagement.

nodes.label: RQ-19: Missing metadata is collected from the business areas that hold it, without a central team
nodes.desc: Missing metadata is collected from the business areas that hold it, without a central team re-keying it.

nodes.label: RQ-20: Policing and justice systems can describe shared data with the same core, alongside their
nodes.desc: Policing and justice systems can describe shared data with the same core, alongside their own interoperability layers.

nodes.label: RQ-21: Metadata held in a catalogue platform's own model, such as the Apache Atlas types behind M
nodes.desc: Metadata held in a catalogue platform's own model, such as the Apache Atlas types behind Microsoft Purview, converts to DCAT-AP-UK through a mapping layer, not by re-keying.

nodes.label: RQ-22: A mapping never invents a value. No default description, licence, language, contact name o
nodes.desc: A mapping never invents a value. No default description, licence, language, contact name or classification; a missing value stays missing and is reported.

nodes.label: RQ-23: Precise positions say which reference frame and epoch they are in, how they were observed
nodes.desc: Precise positions say which reference frame and epoch they are in, how they were observed and how uncertain they are, at a stated confidence.

nodes.label: RQ-24: Geospatial records state their coordinate reference system, give resolution with a unit, a
nodes.desc: Geospatial records state their coordinate reference system, give resolution with a unit, and say how the data is represented; geospatial services state the OGC standards they conform to.

nodes.label: RQ-25: A record declares which profile, layers and versions it was written to.
nodes.desc: A record declares which profile, layers and versions it was written to.

nodes.label: RQ-26: A release passes four gates. Reuse is assessed for every new term; every rule is traced to
nodes.desc: A release passes four gates. Reuse is assessed for every new term; every rule is traced to a test; no serious semantic-loss or disclosure defect is open; compatibility is claimed only with evidence.

nodes.label: RQ-27: UK profiles agree which properties are mandatory, recommended and optional, so a record th
nodes.desc: UK profiles agree which properties are mandatory, recommended and optional, so a record that conforms to one is not rejected by another.

nodes.label: RQ-28: Every requirement can be followed from its evidence to the properties, rules, tests, decis
nodes.desc: Every requirement can be followed from its evidence to the properties, rules, tests, decisions and release that meet it.

nodes.label: RQ-29: Partner overlays attach to the core without changing it. Core discovery stays open; overla
nodes.desc: Partner overlays attach to the core without changing it. Core discovery stays open; overlay terms apply only in partner exchanges.
